sentences.text: It is submitted that whole story of prosecution is that the prosecutrix/victim was born on 13.08.2006 and was a student of Class XII.
Her father is a labourer.
Approximately three years prior to the lodging of the FIR, she was studying in Class IX.
On 29.07.2020 at about 10:30 a.m., the prosecutrix sought a lift from a motorcyclist near Dubhiya Turn.
There, she met the appellant Vimal Lodhi, who gave her a lift and dropped her at her school in Devendranagar.

On the following day,
the appellant allegedly met her outside the school premises, spoke to her and obtained her mobile NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18125 3 CRA-316-2026 number.
Thereafter, the appellant and the prosecutrix remained in telephonic contact.

It is further alleged that approximately one year prior to the lodging of the FIR, the appellant invited the prosecutrix to Gunaur, where she went and engaged in physical relations with him at about 1:00 p.m. in a rented room belonging to his friend.
No other person was present in the room at that time.

It is also alleged that on 13.03.2023, about five months prior to the lodging of the FIR, the appellant again established physical relations with the prosecutrix in a rented room belonging to his elder father,
Ramgopal Lodhi, situated at Maruti Nagar, Satna.
The prosecutrix stated that she informed the appellant that her Class XII examinations were ongoing and that she would be unable to meet or speak with him.
The appellant allegedly threatened to circulate her photographs on Instagram if she refused to continue the relationship.
Due to fear, she remained silent for some time.

Subsequently,
she disclosed the incident to her parents and to her elder father's son, and thereafter went to Police Station Devendranagar along with her mother and submitted a written complaint.

On the basis of the said complaint, a case was registered at Crime No. 181/2023 under Sections 376 and 376(2)(N)
of the IPC, Sections 3/4 and 5L/6 of the POCSO Act, and Sections 3(1)(W)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act at Police Station Devendranagar.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the impugned judgment is contrary to law and evidence.

It is contended that the learned Trial Court failed to properly appreciate the material Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194901386/
2 available on record and based the conviction on presumptions and conjectures rather than on cogent and reliable evidence.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

It is a settled principle of criminal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18125 4 CRA-316-2026 jurisprudence that the burden lies entirely upon the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

In the present case,
material contradictions and inconsistencies in the statements of prosecution witnesses create serious doubt regarding the veracity of the prosecution case.
It is further submitted that there was unexplained and inordinate delay in lodging the FIR.
The alleged incidents are stated to have occurred over a prolonged period; however, the complaint was lodged after considerable delay without any satisfactory explanation.
There is no independent corroboration of the allegations.
The prosecution did not produce any independent witness or corroborative material.
The alleged obscene photographs or videos which formed the basis of the threat were neither seized nor produced before the Court.
It is further argued that as per the prosecution case, the relationship continued over a substantial period.
The learned Trial Court failed to consider material contradictions and did not properly evaluate the defence evidence, ignoring significant discrepancies in the prosecution case.
In these circumstances, the appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt and that the conviction and sentence are liable to be set aside.

7. On the other hand, Shri Ajay Tamrakar, learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State,
supported the impugned judgment and submitted that the Trial Court rightly convicted the appellant and that no interference is warranted.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Her date of birth is 13.08.2006.

Her youngest sister was 17 years younger than her.
She also admitted in para 5 of her cross-examination that Ex.D-1 is the Samagra I.D. of her family and the details are mentioned of her family in the Samagra I.D.
In registration of Samagra I.D. dated 27.02.2023, her age was mentioned 18 years.
10. Mother of victim (PW-2) stated in her examination-in-chief that age of victim is 17 years, the date of birth of victim is 13.08.2006.

She admitted in para 7 of her cross-examination that her third child was born in year 2014 and her fifth child is three years old, but she had no knowledge about date of birth of that child, but year is 2020.
11. Smt. Diksha Tripathi (PW-3) stated that she was posted as Headmaster at Government Primary School Dubahiya on 14.09.2023.
She deposed that she gave the certified copy of the admission form regarding the date of birth and copy of scholar register which was seized by police.

at about 10:30 a.m., the victim sought a lift from the accused/appellant Vimal Lodhi, who gave her a lift and dropped her at her School in Devendranagar.
On the next day, she met with accused/appellant outside the school premises and talked to him.

Accused asked her mobile number and she gave her mobile number, then accused/appellant started NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18125 8 CRA-316-2026 talking with victim.

About one year prior to the lodging of the FIR, accused/appellant invited the victim at Gunaur and she went to Gunaur and engaged in physical relations with him at about 1:00 p.m. in a rented room belonging to his friend.

After that on 13.03.2023, five months prior to the lodging of the FIR, the appellant again established physical relations with the prosecutrix in a rented room belonging to his elder father Ramgopal Lodhi situated at Maruti Nagar, Satna.

Her 12th Class examination was going on, therefore, she told to accused/appellant that she would be unable to meet or talk with accused/appellant, then accused/appellant threatened her to circulate her photographs on Instagram if she refused to continue the relationship.

She first disclosed the incident to her parents, then her elder father's son and thereafter went to Police Station Devendranagar along with her mother and submitted a written complaint in Devendranagar Police Station, which is Ex.P-1.
On the basis of such complaint, police registered FIR (Ex.P-2).
She admitted in para 8 of her cross-examination that she went to Gunaur on her own freewill.
From her testimony, it appears that she maintained contact with the accused and voluntarily accompanied him.
The allegation of threat regarding circulation of photographs on Instagram is not supported by any seizure or production of such photographs or electronic material during investigation.

18. Mother of the victim (PW-2) stated that on 17.06.2023 victim told her that Vimal Lodhi tortured her and threatened that if she will not talk to him, then he will upload the photographs of the victim in the Instagram.
She also stated that victim did not say anything apart from said fact.

When this witness declared hostile by the prosecution, then she stated that victim told NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18125 9 CRA-316-2026 her that Vimal Lodhi called her at Gunaur and made physical relationship with victim.

19. Father of victim (PW-11) admitted in para 5 of his cross- examination that victim did not tell him anything regarding the incident and he voluntarily stated that if she had told her mother, he cannot tell.
20.
Dr. Smt. Swarnima Upadhyay (PW-5) stated that she had examined the victim on dated 18.06.2023.
As per her opinion, it is not possible to give any definite opinion regarding immediate sexual intercourse.
As per her evidence, it is also appear that victim genitals shows no sign of internal or external injury, the hymen was torn in several directions.
21. From the evidence of Dr. Dushyant Prakash Patel (PW-4), it appears that he had examined the competency of accused person and he found that accused was competent to commit intercourse.
His MLC report is Ex.P-13.
DNA report is negative.

DNA report is Ex.P-27.
22.
Upon analysis of the evidence regarding the age of the victim, material contradictions are evident.

The school register records her date of birth as 08.05.2005, whereas the municipal birth Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194901386/
5 certificate records it as 13.08.2006.

The Samagra ID indicates her age as 18 years in 2023.
23.

After analyzing the evidence which was produced by the prosecution on the point of age of the victim, it appears that there is many contradictions in the documents regarding the date of birth of the victim because as per School Register victim's date of birth is 08.05.2005 and as per the birth certificate which was issued by Municipal Council Devendranagar, victim's date of birth is 13.08.2006 and as per Samagra I.D. (Ex.P-1), age of the victim NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18125 10 CRA-316-2026 in the year 2023 was 18 years, therefore, it appears that age of the victim on the date of incident was less than 18 years is doubtful.
Victim also admitted that her youngest sister's age is three years and her youngest sister is less than 17 years from her, it appears that the victim age was nearabout 20 years.
It is also appropriate to mention here that the accused age was also 19 years at the time of incident.
The prosecution has not conducted any medical age- determination test to conclusively establish that she was below 18 years on the date of incident.
Thus, the minority of the victim at the relevant time is rendered doubtful.
24. Considering aforesaid evidence, it is evident that the victim was consenting party and her age is doubtful that she was less than 18 years at the time of incident
, therefore, no offence is made out under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC, 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act, 2012 and also there is no offence is proved under Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act.
25. Accordingly, this criminal appeal filed by the appellant is hereby allowed.
Impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by learned trial Court is hereby set aside.

The appellant,
who is in jail, shall be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
26. Record of the trial Court be sent back immediately.
27. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
